name: France
plates: White, black text, blue EU strip on left with 'F'
bollards: Slim white posts with a red or white reflective top band
coverage: Mostly car; matte/soft image quality in rural areas
terrain: Plane trees lining rural roads; red-tiled roofs in the south
tells: Département number often printed at the end of the plate
Wide gravel road shoulders (accotements) are common
Speed limit signs are plain white circles with red border, no photo radar icon

name: Germany
plates: White, black text, blue EU strip with 'D', city code + letters/numbers
bollards: White posts with red/white reflectors, very uniform and well maintained
coverage: Sharp, high-quality car coverage; camera often mounted lower than neighbors
terrain: Immaculate asphalt, dense forest (Wald) signage, half-timbered houses in the south
tells: Yellow diamond priority-road signs are everywhere
Kilometer marker posts are white with black numbers
Google car coverage stops abruptly at some borders due to opt-outs
